Connect dimension tables to the central fact table through one-to-many relationships using the dimension’s unique key.
source_refs: powerbi_docs#https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/star-schema — Star schema relevance to Power BI semantic models

briefs.learning_objective: Learner can define relationships between tables within a BI tool's data model so visuals can query across them correctly.

required_facts.statement: Model relationships propagate filters between related tables so a visual can use fields from multiple tables.
Use Modeling > Manage relationships > New and choose the two tables and their matching columns.
Set cardinality according to the uniqueness of values on each side and check the active relationship setting.
Choose cross-filter direction deliberately: Single propagates filters in one direction and Both allows propagation in both directions.

briefs.learning_objective: Learner can design a Power BI dashboard/report page laying out visuals to answer a stakeholder's reporting needs.

required_facts.statement: A Power BI report page contains visuals that communicate information from the model; a service dashboard is a separate collection of tiles.
In report view, choose fields from the Data pane and a visual type from Visualizations to add a visual to the canvas.
source_refs: powerbi_docs#https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/visuals/power-bi-report-add-visualizations — Add visualizations to a Power BI report

required_facts.statement: Arrange important information prominently and keep the page focused on the audience’s question.
source_refs: powerbi_docs#https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/service-dashboards-design-tips — Consider your audience; Tell a story on one screen

required_facts.statement: Choose comparisons and trends appropriate to the need, avoid clutter, and keep display choices consistent.
source_refs: powerbi_docs#https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/service-dashboards-design-tips — Use the right visualization for the data

briefs.learning_objective: Learner can design a Tableau dashboard laying out visuals to answer a stakeholder's reporting needs.

required_facts.statement: A Tableau dashboard combines views from worksheets in one place.

Build a worksheet bar chart by dragging a category dimension to Rows and a numeric measure to Columns (or vice versa), using Bar as the mark type; these field placements create the category/value view that can be placed on the dashboard.
source_refs: tableau_help#https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/buildexamples_bar.htm — Build a Bar Chart — introductory field arrangements

required_facts.statement: Select New Dashboard and drag sheets from the dashboard pane onto the canvas.
Choose a dashboard size suited to how the audience will view it, and arrange the most important view prominently.
source_refs: tableau_help#https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/dashboards_best_practices.htm — Set an appropriate size; Place the most important view at the top-left

required_facts.statement: Limit the number of views to keep the dashboard focused and readable.

briefs.learning_objective: Learner can apply visual design principles (chart selection, layout, color, decluttering) to make dashboards readable and accurate.

required_facts.statement: Use chart types that fit the question: bars support category comparisons and lines support trends over time.
source_refs: powerbi_docs#https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/visuals/power-bi-visualization-types-for-reports-and-q-and-a — Charts for comparison and trends — Bar and column charts; Line charts

required_facts.statement: Place important information where readers are likely to notice it and keep the layout focused.
source_refs: powerbi_docs#https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/service-dashboards-design-tips — Tell a story on one screen

required_facts.statement: Use color consistently and avoid unnecessary variety or decoration that distracts from the data.
source_refs: powerbi_docs#https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/service-dashboards-design-tips — Use the right visualization for the data

required_facts.statement: Reduce unnecessary views and labels so the intended comparison remains readable.
source_refs: tableau_help#https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/dashboards_best_practices.htm — Limit the number of views; Make it easy to read

briefs.learning_objective: Learner can publish and share a finished BI report/dashboard with stakeholders through the appropriate delivery mechanism (e.g. Power BI Service).

required_facts.statement: Publish a Desktop report with Home > Publish and choose a destination workspace in the Power BI service.
source_refs: powerbi_docs#https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/desktop-upload-desktop-files — Publish semantic models and reports from Power BI Desktop

required_facts.statement: Select Share for a report or dashboard and specify recipients or an appropriate sharing link.
Choose whether recipients can reshare or build on the underlying data and grant only the permissions the audience needs.
Sharing and access depend on license and capacity; sharing generally requires Pro or PPU, and free recipients require eligible Premium or Fabric capacity.

briefs.learning_objective: Learner can write DAX measures and calculated columns in Power BI to compute business metrics.

required_facts.statement: A DAX measure calculates a result that changes with the current report filtering and selection context.
Use Modeling > New measure and enter MeasureName = SUM(TableName[NumericColumn]) to define a basic total that responds to report context.
A calculated column uses a DAX expression to calculate a value for each row rather than the measure’s report-context result.
Use New Column and write column_name = expression; the formula is applied across the table’s rows.
In standard Import mode, calculated-column values are materialized and refreshed when the underlying data is refreshed.

For a classic date-column time-intelligence calculation, use a marked date table whose Date or date/time column contains unique, nonblank dates without gaps and spans full years, including the periods being compared.
Relate the date table to the metric table’s relevant date column with an active relationship so that report filters on the date table propagate to the metric’s rows.
source_refs: powerbi_docs#https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/relationships-active-inactive — Active relationships; Inactive relationships — active OrderDate relationship and filter propagation

required_facts.statement: Evaluate the base total measure in the current date filter context and obtain its corresponding prior-year value with PriorYear = CALCULATE([MeasureName], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Date'[Date])), which evaluates that measure with the dates shifted one year back.

Compute year-over-year growth with Growth = DIVIDE([MeasureName] - [PriorYear], [PriorYear]) and format it as a percentage; without an alternate result, DIVIDE returns BLANK when the prior-year denominator is zero or blank.
source_refs: powerbi_docs#https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/best-practices/dax-divide-function-operator — DIVIDE syntax and zero or BLANK denominator behavior

briefs.learning_objective: Learner can write Tableau calculated fields to compute derived business metrics within a workbook.

required_facts.statement: A Tableau calculated field derives new data from existing fields without changing the original source.
Choose Analysis > Create Calculated Field, name the field, enter an expression, and select OK.
The source’s Discount Ratio calculation is IIF([Sales] !=0, [Discount]/[Sales],0): it returns Discount divided by Sales when Sales is nonzero, and zero otherwise.
source_refs: tableau_help#https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/calculations_calculatedfields_create.htm — Create a calculated field — Discount Ratio example

required_facts.statement: A basic calculation may operate at the row level or at the visualization’s aggregate level, depending on its expression.
Numeric calculated fields can be summed automatically when added to a view; change the aggregation if the intended metric requires a different one.
source_refs: tableau_help#https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/calculations_calculatedfields_create.htm — Use a calculated field in the view

briefs.learning_objective: Learner can build a centralized semantic layer (shared measure/field definitions) so multiple reports reuse one consistent business logic.

required_facts.statement: A Power BI semantic model contains data-model logic that can be used to build reports.
Reports can reuse an existing published semantic model rather than each creating separate data and calculation definitions.
source_refs: powerbi_docs#https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/service-datasets-across-workspaces — Discover semantic models; Copy a report

required_facts.statement: Define the shared business calculation as a measure in the common model and use that model for reports that need the same calculation.
Connect a new report to the existing shared semantic model; building content on a shared model requires Build permission.
source_refs: powerbi_docs#https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/service-datasets-across-workspaces — Discover semantic models; Build permission for semantic models
